quizzes.stem: A gate in a support agent's dispatcher refuses a refund because no identity has been verified. What should the dispatcher send back to the model?

options.a: A flagged failure result that names the missing step
options.b: Nothing, because an unanswered call simply ends the turn
options.c: A generic error that says only that the call failed
options.d: The refund's result after running the verification itself

explanation.a: Every call needs an answer, and an error that names the missing step lets the model do it and try again.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the API requires a result: "Tool result blocks must immediately follow their corresponding tool use blocks in the message history."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the documentation's advice is to "include what went wrong and what Claude should try next".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model must obtain the code from the customer: "the gate refuses and says what is missing".

quizzes.stem: On a model that supports forced tool use, a team forces the verification tool through tool_choice on the first request, believing the order of steps is now guaranteed. Which gap remains?

options.a: Later tools can stay blocked until verification returns a result
options.b: Text written before the call changes the order in which the tools run
options.c: Later turns are unconstrained, so a refund can still follow a failed check
options.d: The forced choice makes the system prompt uncached, so the cost rises

explanation.c: A forced choice applies to the request that sets it, and nothing carries it to later calls.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the model writes no text before a forced call: "the API prefills the assistant message to force a tool to be used".
explanation.a: Ruled out because keeping later tools blocked until verification returns is what a gate does, not what a forced choice does: "An order between steps is a property of the program that runs them."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the system prompt stays cached: "tool definitions and system prompts remain cached".

quizzes.stem: A refund gate becomes stricter after three failed identity checks: it now refuses every protected step. A locked-out customer's chat loops until the turn limit. What went wrong?

options.a: The lock should have waited for ten failures instead of three
options.b: The route to a person depended on the same safeguard that had tripped
options.c: The turn limit should have been set a lot lower, so that the loop ended sooner
options.d: The model should have been asked to hand the case over on its own

explanation.b: An escape route must not sit behind a prerequisite that may be what failed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the lock is not the fault: "a successful check resets the count, so ordinary typing mistakes do not lock anyone out".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a lower limit only shortens a dead end: "An agent that cannot verify identity and is also barred from escalating is a dead end that loops until the turn limit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model has no route to a person while escalation sits behind the prerequisite: "if every tool is behind the prerequisite, a blocked agent can only loop."

quizzes.stem: A refund over the limit is escalated with the full chat transcript attached, and reviewers spend minutes finding what was verified and what was blocked. Which change helps most?

options.a: Keep the transcript, but have the model highlight its key lines
options.b: Attach a model-written summary of the conversation beside the full transcript
options.c: Add the customer's complete order history to the escalation
options.d: Send a gate-built record, with the agent's reason as one field

explanation.d: The gate holds the facts, and a record answers the reviewer's questions in a fixed place.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A summary written by the model can leave out what went wrong."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a record carries only what is needed: "identifiers and amounts, not the whole order contents".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the model is again choosing what the reviewer sees: "The gate's state is the source for what was verified, looked up and refunded; the model's account of them is not."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A gate verified customer A earlier in a session. Now someone presents another identity code for customer B, and the check fails. What should the gate's state say next?

options.a: Customers A and B are both verified, because the new check adds evidence
options.b: Customer A is still verified, since an earlier check succeeded
options.c: No one is cleared, so every protected step is refused again
options.d: Customer A stays verified until the model confirms which one is meant

explanation.c: A failed check clears the verified customer.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a failed verification clears the state, so that an earlier success cannot be reused."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the state holds one verified customer, and a failure does not add one: "set only by a successful verification call".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the gate does not consult the model about its own state: "does not ask the model whether it did".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A policy allows refunds only for items that arrived damaged. The team encodes "damaged" as a keyword list in the gate, and many valid claims are refused. Which fix fits best?

options.a: Keep extending the keyword list until the valid claims finally pass through it
options.b: Let the model weigh the evidence, and keep steps, amounts and limits as rules
options.c: Move the refund limit into the prompt as well, so that the gate has fewer rules
options.d: Drop the ownership check altogether, so that more claims reach the model

explanation.b: Judgement is the model's work, and rules with a right answer are the gate's.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A design that puts judgement in code ends up with a brittle rule engine".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the thresholds and the order of steps go in the gate".
explanation.d: Ruled out because ownership is a rule with a right answer: "Everything above it is a rule with a right answer, which code checks the same way every time."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A team tests its refund gate by running five hundred live conversations, counts zero skipped verifications and ships. What is still missing?

options.a: A judge model that grades every single conversation for the order of its steps in it
options.b: A larger live sample, since zero in five hundred proves the rate is zero
options.c: The same live run with the verification rule written in capitals
options.d: Direct checks that make the forbidden call and assert it never hits the backend

explanation.d: The gate is code, so it is tested with the forbidden call and an assertion on the backend log.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a sample measures a rate, which is the way the model is tested: "where a failure is a rate and not a bug".
explanation.c: Ruled out because capitals only change the text the model weighs: "text that the model reads and weighs with everything else in its context".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the gate is tested the way all code is: "the same inputs, the same outputs".
